meta.description: Ten ways to ask a question, a live quiz, ten simulations and a Linux terminal.

entete.accroche: The teacher prepares the quiz. The link opens in a browser, on a school computer or elsewhere. A code or a QR code leads to the same link.

studio.titre: Ten ways to ask a question.
studio.texte: Single choice, multiple choice, true or false, short answer, number, fill-in-the-blank, matching, order, a zone on an image, free answer.
points: A question can carry an image, a sound or a video.
At their own pace, each student opens the quiz with the link, the code or the QR code.
Live, the class answers together. A wrong answer scores nothing. A right answer scores more when it arrives early. The server keeps the time.
When the school turns AI on, it suggests questions. The teacher reviews them before opening them to students. Without an AI key, the feature is off.

jeux.texte: Tri Cyber, Nœuds Réseaux, Labo des seuils, Pilote des stocks, Sprint Agile, Robot Route, Requête Parfaite, Ordonnanceur CPU, Budget ERP, Labo Big-O. Each simulation has three challenges.

cartes.texte: A Linux terminal is for practising commands.
Individually, each student plays on a phone. Together, the Linux terminal is shown on the board: the teacher types a command, or picks the one a student sends.
